Discovery must establish the endpoint, clients, runtime versions, configuration, store ownership and lifetime, identity and access behavior, shared state, concurrency and restart behavior before these choices can guide implementation and tests; absent contrary evidence, the recorded default is no new identity, persistence, or cross-process sharing, which rules out adding those capabilities. S2 — Fact: add name filtering and pagination to the user list endpoint with tests, without unrelated scope; discovery must first establish the existing API, response shape, validation, test conventions, and runtime guarantees to resolve parameter names and shapes, matching rules, pagination limits and end conditions, invalid inputs, status codes, errors, visibility, and test seams, which block a compatible implementation and boundary checks. Where evidence does not settle a choice, the recorded default is to preserve existing unfiltered behavior when options are omitted, follow existing conventions, and choose the smallest compatible behavior; an option requiring a person-only decision remains open, while other work proceeds.
